status: DRAFT for review. Maps USDA FoodData Central NAMES (plus record attributes) of the category 'Legumes and Legume Products' to candidate lexicon rows of kind whole_food. It never decides a NOVA group: FDC supplies naming evidence only; placement comes from the FAO clause.

clause.text: legumes such as beans, lentils, and chickpeas
clause.where: FAO 2019 (Monteiro et al., Ultra-processed foods, diet quality, and health using the NOVA classification system), Table 1, Group 1 examples, p. 11
clause.scope: The clause is unconditioned and names a CLASS (legumes) with three examples. It places legumes as foods of the first group: the Group 1 definition (FAO p.6) covers dried, ground, cracked, roasted, boiled and similar minimal processing, but adds no salt, sugar, oil, fat or other substance. A plain dry or raw legume is an instance of the class. Anything that is a product made from a legume (tofu, tempeh, miso, milk, butter, sauce, flour, protein fraction, canned in brine, cooked with sauce) is not an instance of this clause.

acceptance: A1. The FDC food category is exactly 'Legumes and Legume Products'.
A2. The name states a PLAIN seed form: a form part 'raw', 'dry' or 'mature seeds, raw' (SR Legacy), or the Foundation pattern 'Beans, Dry, <variety> (0% moisture)'.
A3. The name holds no word from the word guard (below), no product word and no queue word.
A4. The record attributes do not contradict the plain form: no portion description/modifier of the record holds a guard word (a record named 'raw' whose portions say 'cooked' goes to QUEUE).
A5. The derived label term is a distinct food name (not a bare colour or a pod-vs-seed ambiguity): else QUEUE.

A6. Canonical deduplication: preparation, cut, grade and cultivar-shade variants of one food collapse into ONE row (table 'canonical' below); the others are reported as synonym CANDIDATES (synonyms.csv is not touched in this workstream).

word_guard.why: The category-wide extension of the Spices and Herbs word guard (owner rule 3 for class batches): any treatment, addition, canning/cooking liquid, brand-style or product descriptor puts the name outside a plain dry/raw seed. A guard word anywhere in the name = REJECT (processed). 'plain' and 'original' are guarded because they only occur in product names (soy milk, tofu, yogurt) in this category.
word_guard.note_light: 'light' is NOT guarded: in this category it is a colour shade of a bean ('Light Red Kidney', 'Light Tan'); the reduced-fat sense is caught by 'lite', 'low' and 'reduced'.

product_words.why: A product made from a legume (or a brand/series name) is not the legume: REJECT (product). It is neither an instance of the FAO legumes clause nor a plain single ingredient.

queue_words.peanut: overlaps the CONDITIONED FAO nuts/seeds clause ('tree and ground nuts and other oily seeds (with no added salt or sugar)'); FDC files peanuts under Legumes. Boundary and kind (nut_seed) belong to the Nut and Seed batch.
queue_words.flour: a flour is placed by the 'flours' class (PMC10127522 fn2, NUPENS), not by the legumes clause; kind flour belongs to the flour batch (Cereal Grains and Pasta: plain flours).
queue_words.meal: defatted/ground fraction: not established as a plain flour or a whole legume.
queue_words.defatted: a fractionated (defatted) form: composition changed by an industrial step; not an instance of the plain legume clause.
queue_words.carob: carob is not a Group 1 legume example of the clause (a pod used as a cocoa substitute); no source read places it.
queue_words.soy: 'soy' forms other than the plain raw seed are products; see the product words.

generic_queue.why: A bare colour or pod-versus-seed name does not establish a distinct food: 'brown/tan/light tan/red/small red/medium red beans' are Foundation market-class colour labels of Phaseolus vulgaris; 'french beans' and 'yellow beans' on an Indian label usually denote the fresh pod (a vegetable); 'white beans' is a generic of cannellini/navy/great northern. QUEUE (conditional on a label that names the food).
